name: f-verb-low

content.text: Explain how a bicycle stays upright.

data.text:
A bicycle stays upright mainly because it can **steer itself back under its falling side**. If it starts tipping left, the front wheel tends to turn left; that moves the wheels’ support back beneath the bike and helps it recover. A rider does this consciously too, making constant small steering corrections.

The front fork’s angle and **trail** (where the steering axis meets the ground relative to the tire contact point) help the wheel steer in a stabilizing way. The spinning wheels’ gyroscopic effect can contribute, but it isn’t the whole explanation—some bicycles can be designed to balance without relying on it.

At very low speeds, there’s less time and motion for these corrections, so balancing gets harder.
